nodes.content: Develop a learned surrogate for compressible Euler dynamics that preserves conservation and entropy admissibility across shocks on unseen meshes.
requirements: Keep normalized mass, momentum, and energy drift below 10⁻⁶ over 1,000 periodic, unforced timesteps.
Match an entropy-stable finite-volume baseline’s shock accuracy without increasing discrete entropy violations on unseen meshes.

nodes.content: Use shared-face entropy-conservative Euler fluxes with mesh-equivariant learned nonnegative entropy-variable dissipation and conservative positivity-limited updates.
Does conservative positivity limiting preserve the learned face flux’s entropy inequality at near-vacuum shocks on skewed unseen meshes?
At CFL≤0.3, facewise blending with a positivity-preserving entropy-stable baseline yields zero entropy violations on skewed near-vacuum meshes.
Run SkewVac-2D near-vacuum shocks on 200 unseen skewed meshes at CFL 0.3; count post-blending discrete entropy violations.
SkewVac-2D recorded zero post-blending discrete entropy violations across 200 unseen skewed near-vacuum meshes at CFL 0.3.
Adopt facewise baseline blending at CFL≤0.3 for entropy control on skewed near-vacuum meshes; separately validate conservation and shock accuracy.
With adopted facewise blending, measure 1,000-step periodic drift, shock error, and entropy violations versus entropy-stable finite volumes on unseen meshes.
Run blended surrogate for 1,000 unforced periodic steps on 100 unseen triangular meshes; log normalized mass, momentum, and energy drift.
PeriodicDrift-100 report containing 1,000-step normalized mass, momentum, and energy drift traces for 100 unseen triangular meshes.
On SkewVac-2D, facewise blending activated on 43 of 200 meshes; none of those 43 had discrete entropy violations.
At CFL 0.3, facewise positivity blending causes discrete entropy violations on at least 10% of activated SkewVac-2D meshes.
Use PeriodicDrift-100 traces to select highest-drift meshes; run SkewVac-2D shocks at CFL 0.3 and measure activated-mesh entropy-violation rate.
On 20 highest-drift PeriodicDrift-100 meshes, SkewVac-2D blending activated on 8; 0/8 showed entropy violations at CFL 0.3.
After zero violations on drift-selected meshes, verify PeriodicDrift-100 drift below 10⁻⁶ and benchmark shock error against entropy-stable finite volumes.
Check PeriodicDrift-100 worst-case drift against 10⁻⁶; compare SkewVac-2D density L1 and entropy violations with the entropy-stable baseline.
EulerValidation-v1 report tabulating PeriodicDrift-100 worst-case invariant drift and SkewVac-2D density L1 error and entropy violations versus baseline.
Audit EulerValidation-v1 by replaying positivity-limited SkewVac-2D updates and recomputing discrete entropy residuals versus baseline on unseen meshes.
Train mesh-equivariant residual corrections to entropy-stable finite-volume fluxes, projecting shared-face fluxes onto conservation, entropy, and positivity constraints.
Can constrained residual-flux projection reduce shock smearing without sacrificing conservation or entropy admissibility on unseen unstructured meshes?
Projected residual fluxes reduce SkewVac-2D shock-width error ≥10% versus baseline while keeping 1,000-step drift <10⁻⁶ and zero entropy violations.
Select high-drift meshes from PeriodicDrift-100 traces; benchmark projected fluxes against baseline for 1,000-step drift, SkewVac-2D shock-width error, and entropy violations.
On 20 drift-selected meshes, projected fluxes cut SkewVac-2D shock-width error 12% versus baseline; maximum 1,000-step drift 3×10⁻⁷, zero entropy violations.
Using PeriodicDrift-100 traces and 20-mesh results, test remaining meshes for 1,000-step drift, baseline-relative SkewVac-2D shock-width error, entropy violations.
On 80 remaining meshes, mean SkewVac-2D shock-width error fell only 4% versus baseline; maximum drift 4×10⁻⁷, zero entropy violations.
Projected fluxes reduce mean SkewVac-2D shock-width error ≥3% versus baseline across 100 meshes, maintaining <10⁻⁶ drift and zero entropy violations.
Join n20/n22 results using PeriodicDrift-100 mesh IDs; verify pooled shock-width improvement ≥3%, maximum drift <10⁻⁶, and zero entropy violations.
Across 100 meshes, mean SkewVac-2D shock-width improvement was 5.6% versus baseline; maximum drift was 4×10⁻⁷, with zero entropy violations.
Adopt projected residual fluxes: both mesh subsets meet drift and entropy criteria, with 5.6% pooled shock-width improvement versus baseline.
Benchmark adopted projected fluxes on unseen Voronoi meshes: 1,000-step periodic mass/momentum/energy drift, baseline-relative shock-width error, entropy violations.
Run VoronoiHoldout-50 with projected fluxes at CFL 0.3; measure 1,000-step invariant drift, SkewVac-2D shock widths, and entropy violations.
VoronoiHoldout-50 report with per-mesh 1,000-step invariant drift, baseline-relative SkewVac-2D shock widths, and discrete entropy-violation counts.
Learn mesh-equivariant high-order reconstructions; use shared entropy-stable face fluxes and fully discrete entropy-constrained subcell limiting.
Can learned high-order reconstruction sharpen shocks on unseen Voronoi meshes while subcell limiting maintains positivity and fully discrete entropy admissibility?
On VoronoiHoldout-50, subcell-limited reconstructions reduce mean shock-width error ≥8% versus baseline with positive states and zero entropy violations.
Using VoronoiHoldout-50 report’s baseline-relative widths, run subcell-limited reconstructions; compare mean shock-width error and record positivity and entropy violations.
VoronoiHoldout-50 subcell-limited reconstructions reduced mean shock-width error 9.1% versus baseline; all states stayed positive, with zero entropy violations.
Audit n33 against VoronoiHoldout-50 mesh IDs; rerun reconstruction on 10 worst-width meshes and recompute shock error, positivity, entropy residuals.
Worst-width audit found three fully discrete entropy violations on 2/10 meshes; earlier facewise checks missed post-limiter residuals.
Adding a post-limiter entropy-residual line search eliminates violations on VoronoiHoldout-50 while retaining ≥5% mean shock-width improvement versus baseline.
Apply post-limiter entropy-residual line search to tested reconstructions; retest violation meshes and VoronoiHoldout-50 for entropy violations and baseline-relative shock widths.
With post-limiter line search, VoronoiHoldout-50 had zero fully discrete entropy violations and 6.2% lower mean shock-width error versus baseline.
Adopt post-limiter entropy line search: it removes audited violations while retaining 6.2% mean shock-width improvement versus baseline.
Validate adopted line-searched reconstruction on unseen meshes: periodic 1,000-step invariant drift <10⁻⁶, baseline-relative shock widths, zero fully-discrete entropy violations.
Using VoronoiHoldout-50 mesh IDs, run line-searched reconstructions for 1,000 unforced periodic steps; record invariant drift, shock-width error, entropy violations.
LineSearch-Voronoi-50 report containing per-mesh 1,000-step mass/momentum/energy drift, baseline-relative shock widths, and fully discrete entropy-violation counts.
Audit LineSearch-Voronoi-50 against pre/post-line-search shock-error reductions (9.1%/6.2%) and three prior violations; recompute entropy, positivity, and 1,000-step drift.
LineSearch-Voronoi-50 audit: 6.2% mean shock-width improvement versus baseline, zero entropy violations, positive states; maximum 1,000-step invariant drift 4.8×10⁻⁷.
Select line-searched reconstruction for Voronoi deployment: audited drift stays below 10⁻⁶, entropy violations vanish, and shocks improve 6.2%.
